validators.verdict: This resumed run did not start any second copy of a job. No python job of this task was still running (the only python processes were two unrelated fake_coli.py web servers), and the previous attempt had already finished both held-out halves (results\heldout_A.jsonl and heldout_B.jsonl, 360 rows each, last written 20:41). Checked on resume: 720/720 rows present (40 test experts = team 3's set [1,7,9,...,159] x 18 configs), 0 duplicates, 0 decode errors, all source sha256 OK, 0 ceil fallbacks. Every record decodes from bytes alone: byte-exact for the 12 non-c configs (480/480) and value-exact (-0 -> +0) for the 6 c configs (240/240). The WNR2 records are identical to team 3's (total, used, model_id 40/40). The model checks also pass: WNR2 model == team 3 even.npz, and count cross-checks vs team 3 and vs mxceil.py are 80/80 true. Real mean record bytes (4096-aligned), with raw = 18,800,640: WNR2 16,909,926.4 (0.89943); f 16,578,764.8 (0.88182, -1.761% of raw, CI -1.948..-1.632); fg 0.88179 (-1.764%); fgd 0.88039 (-1.905%); fgde 0.88048 (-1.895%); fgdt (tail seeding instead of e) 0.87827 (-2.116%); fga 0.88232 (-1.711%); fgaK2 0.88221 (-1.722%); fgc 0.85439 (-4.504%); fgcde 0.85309 (-4.634%). Increments, measured on unpadded bytes: d -25.8 KB (-0.137%); e +1,352 B; tail seeding -40.2 KB (-0.214%), so tail instead of hash = -41.5 KB (-0.221%); the 3-valued a costs +10.6 KB (+0.057%) and is worse on all 40 experts; K=2 on top of a gives -2.1 KB; c -514.8 KB (-2.738%). g as defined is a wash: -853 B, CI -17.0 KB..+15.1 KB. The reason is that both anchor rules flip once on ceil-form. The f median gives 120 instead of 121 on L24_E058 w1 (costs 217 KB). The densest-pair rule gives 121 on L39_E156 w2, a near tie (pair sums 349,985 vs 350,076), which costs 205-209 KB. A constant anchor of 120 (g0) is what every one of the 240 training matrices and 119/120 test matrices already use. Measured: g0 gives fg -1.791%, fgdt 0.87800 (-2.144%), fgcde 0.85282 (-4.661%), and g0 vs f = -6.0 KB (CI -17.0..-0.5 KB). The f-only cross-check holds. Real delta -331,067 B vs the code-length estimate with the same models on the same experts -331,072 B (difference 5 B, CI -17..+26). An independent estimate from the mxceil counts on the same 40 experts gives -331,088 B. Flush overhead cancels in the delta: same 19,440 streams, real flush = estimate - 0.50 B/stream (about 3.5 B). The quoted -1.81% is the all-160 / odd-80 figure (-1.803% / -1.846% in that estimate); the 40-expert test set is -1.761%, so the 0.045 pp gap comes from which experts are in the set, not from coding overhead. Fallback path tested in memory on L00_E113. A block with max 0, or an even block with scale 254, clears F and the record still decodes byte-exact. Scale 253 keeps F. A forged F flag on a plain record is rejected. A fallback record coded with the ceil-trained model costs +397 KB vs WNR2 on that expert.

validators.verdict: The ceil-form inverse runs byte-exact inside the GPU rANS decoder on the RTX 3070 (sm_86). Across 3 independent paired runs with 41 rounds each, every non-diagnostic variant produced weight and scale slabs equal to the ORIGINAL safetensors bytes. That covers 8 launch configs (nt 32/64/128/256 x plain-store 'lb' / team-2 'out4'), 4 launch patterns and the full GPU pipeline (scale-stream decode, then weight decode with in-place scale fix-up): 352 checks in the final run, 0 bad streams and 0 invariant errors. The negative controls fail as they should (inverse off: 138,240/138,240 weight streams wrong; weight-only inverse: all 138,240 scale groups wrong). Bytes on team 2's 8 experts (in-sample model trained on all 160 experts, flush 4 B/stream): A259 16,963,218 B/record = 0.90227 of raw, ceil-form CF 16,573,694 B/record = 0.88155 (-2.30% of record, -2.07% of raw). That is weights 3.7917 -> 3.7079 bit/w plus scale streams 155,361 -> 136,654 B/record. CFD (+ sign bypass) is 0.88156 and CFDB2 0.88477 (-2.29% vs DB2). The A259, D and DB2 encodings are byte-identical in size to team 2's, which validates the copy. Cost depends on how the scale is fixed. The nibble LUT on the 4 register words is free: CF3/CF0 median 0.995-0.999. The literal per-block 1-byte scale store (CF, CEIL=1) is expensive: +0.3..+21%, median +15.7% for 1 record. The deferred variant (CF5) keeps a 64-bit mask per stream and rewrites at most 4 aligned 16-B scale words at the stream end. Its medians vs the same streams with the inverse off are +1.7% (1 matrix), +0.7% (1 record), +0.3% (8 records), range -2.4..+3.4%. Against A259 at the same config CF5 is 0.988-1.014 (median). Best-config times (final run): 1 matrix A259 300.0 / CF5 304.1 / D 280.6 / CFD5 276.5 / DB2 271.4 / CFDB2 270.3 us. 1 record A259 590.8 / CF5 565.2 / D 523.3 / CFD5 540.7 / DB2 415.7 / CFDB2 431.1 us. 8 records in one launch A259 4171.8 / CF5 4185.1 / D 3835.9 / CFD5 3848.2 / DB2 3230.7 / CFDB2 3307.5 us. The inverse adds 0 B of shared memory and 0-7 registers (CFDB2 +8-10 at nt128/256 lb, which costs occupancy 40->36/32 warps). The scale-stream GPU decoder adds ~45 us per record. The 5090 transfer is uncertain: one record there is ~3 warps/SM (latency-bound, like the 1-matrix case here, where CF5 costs about +1.7%), the L2 and store behaviour differ, and KAIRA's kernel (cp.async ring, 567 rows) is a different code base.

findings.claim: The ceil-form inverse is byte-exact on the GPU against the ORIGINAL safetensors weight and scale bytes, for every stream and every launch config tested.

findings.claim: The nibble LUT itself (magnitudes 0..5 -> 0,2,4,5,6,7, sign kept, applied to the 4 u32 register words when the running block max == 5) costs nothing measurable.
findings.evidence: SWAR f(m)=m+min(m,2): wnr2dec.cu:183-188, applied at wnr2dec.cu:310-315. Paired CF3/CF0 (same ceil streams, inverse on vs off), final run, 8 configs, min/median/max: m1 0.987/0.995/1.010, m3 0.991/0.997/1.007, m24 0.972/0.998/1.003, 8streams 0.964/0.999/1.003.

findings.claim: Writing the corrected scale byte per transformed block inside the block loop (the literal spec, CEIL=1) is expensive. A deferred end-of-stream patch (64-bit even mask, at most 4 aligned 16-B read-modify-writes per lane) brings the cost to about 0-2%.
findings.impact: Use the deferred mask form (or full-slab write) in production, not per-block byte stores. The mask form also allows folding the fix-up into KAIRA's commit kernel, which already copies every scale byte (WNR2-REFERENCE.md:431); that fusion was not measured.

findings.claim: Robustness caveat: the SWAR scale decrement in ceil_fix borrows into the neighbouring byte if a decoded transformed scale byte is 0. Valid data cannot produce this (transformed scale = original + 1 >= 1), but a corrupted stream could.
findings.evidence: wnr2dec.cu:208-211 uses plain u32 subtraction 'v.x -= ...'. __vsub4, or a validity check (bad |= transformed block with scale byte 0), would close it.

validators.verdict: I could not break ceil-form, but its headline gain is overstated by about 0.27 points. What holds (measured). The invariant held on every record checked: 236 records (160 sample, 70 extra routed covering all 40 layers, 6 MTP), 260,997,120 blocks, 0 blocks with max magnitude below 6, 0 with stored max 5, 0 all-zero. The byte round trip failed on 0 of 708 matrices, and the scale range was 112..126 (no 0, 254 or 255). The real rANS coder decoded 17/17 records exactly, both with and without the x0 hash, and T^-1 reproduced the WEX1-layout file byte for byte. The exact bijection condition is narrower than the brief says: 'no stored block with max == 5', not 'max < 6'. Adding 'skip T when scale == 255' makes T total on that domain (exhaustive 4-nibble test: 0 collisions, 0 overflow). Expected fallbacks: 0 of 7680 (95% upper bound 100 records, rule of three on 230 routed records). What is overstated (measured, held-out). The quoted -1.996% weights / -1.846% record (P2) includes the srel anchor fix: the median anchor flips 120->121 in 43 of 690 routed matrices in today's form but in only 2 of 690 in ceil form. Fixing the anchor alone gives -0.305% weights / -0.272% record. With fixed anchors on both sides, ceil-form gives -1.716% weights and -1.592% of raw (P2); P3 gives -1.731% / -1.601%, P4 -1.717% / -1.592%. The best non-ceil model (3-class side symbol + half + fixed anchor + scale|class) reaches -1.807% / -1.780% / -1.827%, which is 97% of the ceil gain. Ceil-form adds only -0.055..-0.057% of raw on top of it (about 10.5 KB per record), but keeps the 567-row table and no extra stream. A single even-flag bit captures 86%. Per-expert spread under today's median anchor was -0.53..-5.10% (std 0.616); with fixed anchors it is -1.18..-1.82% (std 0.103), 0 of 230 experts worse. What breaks or needs care. (a) MTP experts: the routed-trained model expands them (ratio 1.110 original form, 1.079 ceil form) because MTP w1/w3 scales sit at 113-114, so they would be stored raw. With MTP-own models, the median anchor makes ceil worse on MTP layer 0 (+0.14% of raw); with the anchor rule pair(original)+1, all 3 MTP layers gain (-1.25/-1.53/-1.40%). (b) Without the hash, the silent single-sign-flip hole widens: w2 0.29% -> 0.58% of random bit flips accepted, w1 0.26% -> 0.34%. No damage amplification: after T^-1 every accepted flip is still one sign flip with 0 scale changes. (c) GPU: the final scale (ts - 1 when the block max is 5) is known only after the weight block is decoded. The weight kernel must write it to a separate output. Patching the const __restrict__ / __ldg scales buffer in place is undefined behaviour and makes retries non-idempotent. srel and the median ordering are unchanged, and there are no partial blocks.

Scales are an input 'const u8* __restrict__ scales' (line 182), read via __ldg per block (237, 244; u16 pairs at 276-286). srel = clamp(scale - med) (240-241, 281-283). Running block max mx (255, 265; wdec2 392, 403). Each block is stored once as uint4 (269, 320-321, 409, 460-461). The anchor is the per-record header median[3] (WNR2-REFERENCE.md:200, 225), so the ceil-form anchor is stored, not recomputed. Ceil-form: srel uses the coded ts (no new dependency); at block end, if mx == 5, remap the 32 nibbles (0..5 -> 0,2,4,5,6,7, sign kept) before the store and write ts - 1 to a SEPARATE scale output. Writing through the const __restrict__ / __ldg buffer is undefined behaviour, and a retry would read patched scales and decode with wrong srel. Anything reading the slab's scale region between the scale kernel and the weight kernel sees +1 scales on 30.6% of blocks.

validators.verdict: The doubled-block artifact was already in DeepSeek's own release, before the REAP/MXFP4 repack. It is also not specific to this checkpoint: it shows up in every MXFP4 checkpoint we measured that came from quantization-aware training (QAT). Measured: 8 upstream experts of deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 @1bae0e1 that REAP pruned (so they are never in the REAP repo) have 27.8-31.6% 'even' blocks. The 4 kept experts are byte-identical to the REAP sample files. All 13 upstream items together: 14,376,960 blocks, block max code 6 = 45.20%, code 7 = 54.80%, below 6 = 0, even = 29.415% (i.i.d. expectation 0.75%). Other checkpoints: V4.1-Flash 29.54%, V4-Flash 25.98%, V4-Pro 23.89%, openai gpt-oss-20b 21.94%, gpt-oss-120b 21.36%, and AMD's Quark re-export of gpt-oss-120b 21.50% (its scales are byte-identical to OpenAI's; only -0 became +0). Checkpoints quantized after training (PTQ) do not have it: AMD DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 0.0049%, RedHatAI GLM-5.3-MXFP4 0.0034%. The invariant (no block max < 6) held in all 9 checkpoints, about 85M blocks. Mechanism (sources read; how the exporter ran is inferred): DeepSeek's quantizer (kernel.py fast_round_scale, 2^ceil(log2(amax/6))) and OpenAI's triton_kernels default ROUND_UP are both ceil rules, so a single pass gives block max 3.0/4.0/6.0. Re-quantizing those already-dequantized values with ceil again, or with the OCP floor rule, moves exactly the max-3.0 blocks to half the scale with every code doubled (3s/6 = s/2 is an exact power of two). It changes nothing else, and it is value-exact. Simulation (my sim_double.json, 400k-block runs): ceil twice and ceil-then-floor give identical codes and scales, block max 6/7 = 51.4/48.6%, even 22.3%. Reading gpt-oss's stored data back to its first pass gives 21.9/52.0/26.1%, against 22.2/51.5/26.3% for a single ceil pass on log-uniform data. The public inference code never quantizes expert weights: convert.py only reinterprets the stored bytes. The OCP MX v1.0 spec §6.3 sets the floor rule but explicitly allows other algorithms. Ceil-form gain with a simple shared base model, held-out by item parity: gpt-oss-20b -1.86% of weight bits (record -1.69% of raw), gpt-oss-120b -1.96% (-1.75%), AMD gpt-oss -2.08% (-1.81%), V4-Flash -1.04% (-1.15%), V4-Pro -0.82% (-0.99%), upstream 1017 -2.25% (-2.14%), PTQ checkpoints about 0. Most of the larger transfer gain comes from ceil-form removing the cost of reusing a model trained on another checkpoint (+4.2% in the original form, +0.3% in ceil-form): the matrix median scale is 120 in V4.1 but 121 in V4/V4-Pro, and ceil-form stabilises it. It should sit behind a per-matrix or per-container flag that is set only when no block has max < 6. A checkpoint quantized once with a ceil rule (for example transformers quantize_to_mxfp4 with its ROUND_UP default) would already contain about 22% max-code-5 blocks (simulated, not seen on a real checkpoint), so the transform must stay off there. That data is already in the compact form.

integration.verdict: I wrote <RESEARCH-PC>\team4\spec-update\WNR3-DRAFT-v2.md (DRAFT 0.2, 70,223 B). It sits next to a byte copy of team 3's draft, and the original is unchanged (sha256 086C4B56...1844BED0 before and after). The container rules stay as they were: WEX3 v3, header flags 32/64, codec 5, entry bits 8-15 now mirror the 8 record flag bits, and table_offset stays 65,536 for the v1 model (K=2, 57,736 B). Ceil-form (f) is now a first-class feature. Its exact per-matrix gate is "no block with max magnitude 5", even blocks with scale 255 are left untransformed, and a matrix that fails the gate falls back to a plain-form table set; coding it with the ceil set instead costs +397,312 B, measured by ceil-ref. The decoder inverse runs on the coded domain after the block max is known, applies the SWAR D(m)=m+min(m,2) before the uint4 store, and writes the final scales deferred into a separate output; in-place patching is forbidden. All hashes are computed on the coded domain. Anchor rule g0 is a constant per set and matrix type: 120 on V4.1, measured at -6,028 B vs f; the densest-pair rule is a wash on ceil-form. Features a (+10,642 B, worse on all 40 experts) and k-means b (+8,585 B on c+d+e) move to an appendix as measured but not adopted; a also needs a 1,211-3,402-row table against 259 rows for v1. For the start-state bits I recommend TAIL+DIGEST: -41,548 B (-0.221% of raw) vs HASH, with the digest at 0 B in a reserved header word. The digest closes the 0.26-0.58% silent sign-flip hole, which TAIL alone would leave open. Sign bypass is an optional layout 2 (1.03e-6 bit/w; -6.5..-11.4% decode time vs A259 on the 3070). It may not be combined with canonical zero, because the fixed sign plane gives back all of c's gain. The canonical-zero section records team 2's 0-differing-bit results, the untested sm_120/Vulkan paths, the required 5090 bit test and per-step logits memcmp, and the tooling breakages. The v1 byte-exact default (CEIL|LENC|TAIL|DIGEST) measured 0.87800 of raw (-2.144% vs WNR2 0.89943); with this spec's layout about 0.8781 (estimate). The value-exact profile measured 0.85282 with e; with t instead about 0.8507 (estimate, not run). I took the measured numbers from the team result files, spot-checking ceil-ref's g0 summary and ceil-gpu's best_final.txt against the files themselves. KAIRA-dependent items are listed as OPEN-K.
